prompt: A trucking company's fuel cost per mile rose 12%, while diesel prices rose 4%. Its fleet's average age went from 4 to 7 years. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Fuel cost per mile has likely risen faster than diesel prices.
options.feedback: This restates the facts without proposing a cause.

options.text: Older trucks are likely burning more fuel per mile.
options.feedback: Right. Fuel cost per mile rose 8 points faster than prices, so efficiency fell, and the fleet aged three years. I'd compare miles per gallon by truck age.

options.text: Diesel price rises probably explain all of the increase.
options.feedback: Diesel rose 4%, but cost per mile rose 12%.

options.text: Drivers are likely taking longer routes to avoid tolls.
options.feedback: Longer routes add miles, but cost per mile would not rise because of them.

explanation: The data shows fuel cost per mile up 12% against 4% for diesel, as the fleet aged from 4 to 7 years. Likely cause: older trucks burn more fuel. To test it, compare miles per gallon by truck age. If old and new trucks match, look at routes, loads or driving habits.
